task:
You want to try NimbusNotes, a note-taking app a colleague recommended.
Sign up for a FREE account — you are not willing to pay or enter any payment
details. You are done when you reach the welcome screen confirming your
workspace is ready. Use any plausible made-up name, email and password.

examples.ui_element: Step 2 'Set up your workspace' preferences page
examples.evidence: These are optional settings I can change later... Let me scroll down to find the continue button.
examples.suggestion: Keep the primary continue/skip action visible above the fold so users don't have to scroll to find how to proceed past optional settings.

examples.evidence: deliberation=5s ... 'All three fields are filled in ... Everything looks correct, so I'll click "Create account"'
examples.suggestion: Provide inline confirmation (checkmarks or field validation) so the user doesn't have to pause to double-check all fields were captured before submitting.

examples.evidence: deliberation=7s before 'Now I'll click "Create account" to move to step 2.'
examples.suggestion: Ensure the primary CTA is visually obvious and confirm field validation state clearly so users don't pause to double-check before submitting.

examples.evidence: deliberation=9s; 'There's a required-looking "Data Processing Agreement" checkbox that's unchecked — I'll need to tick that to continue.'
examples.suggestion: Clearly mark required agreement checkboxes as mandatory with an explicit label/asterisk and inline validation, rather than making the user infer it's 'required-looking'.

examples.evidence: deliberation=4s; 'The defaults look fine and none relate to payment, so I'll leave them and scroll down to find the continue button.'
examples.suggestion: Make the continue button visible without needing to scroll, or indicate that more content/options lie below the fold.

examples.ui_element: 'continue with the free plan for now' text link on 'Choose your plan'
examples.evidence: 'I notice some faint grey text at the bottom: "continue with the free plan for now." That's exactly what I want, even though it's easy to miss.'
examples.suggestion: Make the free-plan option a clearly visible button or high-contrast link of equal prominence, since burying it in faint grey text is a dark-pattern that risks users abandoning or accidentally selecting a paid plan.

examples.ui_element: 'continue with the free plan for now' link
examples.evidence: 'the faint grey "continue with the free plan for now" link at the bottom'
examples.suggestion: Increase contrast and prominence of the free-plan link so it meets accessibility contrast standards and is easily discoverable.

examples.ui_element: 'continue with the free plan for now' link on plan page
examples.evidence: all three are paid, with "Choose Pro" being the big prominent button... Good thing there's a low-key link at the bottom: "continue with the free plan for now."
examples.suggestion: Present the free plan as a clearly visible, equal-weight option rather than a low-key link, since the free tier is a legitimate primary path.

examples.ui_element: 'continue with the free plan for now' link on Choose your plan
examples.evidence: 'I notice small, faint grey text at the bottom that says "continue with the free plan for now." That's exactly what I want, though it's a bit hidden.'
examples.suggestion: Make the free-plan option a clearly visible button or equally weighted choice rather than faint grey text, so users not wanting to pay can find it without hunting.

examples.detail: "…bottom. That's the one I want. Slightly annoying that they've buried the free option in low-contrast text, but I'll click it."

examples.evidence: 'I'm being nudged toward paid plans... It even says "Every plan starts with a 14-day Pro trial," but I don't want to pay or enter payment details.'
examples.suggestion: Clarify whether the free plan requires payment details and present the free tier as a first-class option to avoid dark-pattern nudging toward paid plans.

examples.ui_element: Plan selection cards / 'continue with the free plan for now' link
examples.evidence: 'all three cards are paid plans ($8/$15/$49)... I spot the faint grey "continue with the free plan for now" link at the bottom... Slightly annoying that they've buried the free option in low-contrast text'
examples.suggestion: Surface the free plan as a clearly visible, equal-weight option (e.g., a proper button or card) instead of a low-contrast buried link, since the landing page promised a free account.

examples.ui_element: 'continue with the free plan for now' link on plan.html
examples.evidence: "There's a faint, low-contrast link at the bottom: 'continue with the free plan for now.' That grayed-out text is deliberately hard to notice — sloppy/manipulative UX."
examples.suggestion: Give the free-plan option equal visual weight (a clear, high-contrast button) so users can select it without hunting, avoiding dark-pattern design.

examples.evidence: There's a "Data Processing Agreement" checkbox at the bottom, unchecked... I'll just try clicking the prominent "Continue" button first
examples.suggestion: Position the required consent checkbox above or adjacent to the Continue button so it isn't buried at the bottom below optional toggles.

examples.evidence: "Let me scroll down to find the continue button."
examples.suggestion: Keep the primary Continue action visible without scrolling, e.g. via a sticky footer button.

examples.ui_element: Pre-checked consent checkboxes on 'Set up your workspace'
examples.evidence: '**Product updates** (checked): occasional marketing email. I don't really want this.' and deliberation=9s reading 'these carefully since I'm cautious about privacy'
examples.suggestion: Default marketing/optional data-sharing checkboxes to unchecked (opt-in) rather than pre-checked, to respect privacy expectations and reduce scrutiny burden.

examples.ui_element: 'Data Processing Agreement' checkbox vs optional items
examples.evidence: deliberation=15s: 'The Data Processing Agreement is different from the optional marketing/analytics items — it's a necessary agreement'
examples.suggestion: Visually separate mandatory legal agreements from optional preference toggles (e.g., a distinct section or required-field styling) so users don't have to spend time reasoning about which are necessary.

examples.evidence: 'all three plans cost money ... The big colorful buttons all push paid plans, which makes me a little wary.'
examples.suggestion: Surface the free option alongside paid tiers as an explicit choice so users pursuing a free account aren't made wary that no free path exists.

examples.evidence: I got an error: "Please review your selections." That must be the required Data Processing Agreement checkbox at the bottom.
examples.suggestion: Make the required DPA checkbox visible near the Continue button or scroll to and highlight the offending field on error, with a specific message like 'Please accept the Data Processing Agreement to continue.'

examples.ui_element: 'Create account' button on Create your account form
examples.evidence: At step 8 the page had already changed to page=/permissions.html before the user clicked 'Create account', and the user still says 'Now I'll click "Create account" to move to the next step.'
examples.suggestion: Ensure page transitions align with user actions so the account-creation submit and page navigation are clearly sequenced; avoid advancing the page before the submit click registers.
